bug_semantics: A dependency controls its installed package.json repository and homepage fields. When a user requests repository/homepage columns, npm-check-updates places those strings into a cli-table3 row and prints the row without neutralizing ESC, OSC, CSI, CR, or other terminal control characters. A malicious dependency value therefore reaches the user's terminal and can manipulate terminal-rendered output when ncu is run with the relevant format option.
flaw_origin: Commit 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138 first created the vulnerable repository-display path. In lib/logging.js lines 89-92 it computed repoUrl as getRepoUrl(dep) || '' and appended it directly to the terminal table row; the same commit's new lib/repo-url.js returned a qualifying packageJson.repository string verbatim. Commit c273d79d7ea5daa2cdf9000120c8f5e7f084017b later extended the same unsanitized table mechanism to packageJson.homepage. Refactors and option renames preserved the original repository sink until the fix.
ai_marker: absent: the exact commit object for 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138 names author Jason O'Neill <CreativeTechGuy@users.noreply.github.com> and committer Jason O'Neill <CreativeTechGuy@users.noreply.github.com>; its message is only 'Add repo urls to new --output command', with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xm8c-hvjf-c5q9 (GHSA-xm8c-hvjf-c5q9 / CVE-2026-73035) describes unfiltered terminal-control characters from dependency package.json homepage or repository URL fields reaching ncu --format homepage/repo output through 23.0.2 and identifies b554b84848fc0b08a9d2b3d3db15e351387168cf as the fix; the advisory's structured affected and patched version fields are themselves Unknown.

First-party report https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates/issues/1988 identifies src/lib/logging.ts as the output path and records an offline reproduction in which an OSC title-setting sequence from a dependency homepage appeared unmodified in captured stdout. First-party fix PR https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates/pull/1994 says it fixes #1988.

numactl-prefixed git log -L over the homepageUrl/repoUrl block and reverse git log -S 'getRepoUrl(dep)' across lib/logging.js, src/logging.js, src/logging.ts, and src/lib/logging.ts trace the earliest repository sink to 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138. The -L history distinguishes later changes: c273d79d7ea5daa2cdf9000120c8f5e7f084017b added the homepage branch; a427316534f637f13edbb7b8259557d0d694d6e6 only renamed repositoryLink to repo; subsequent moves/refactors retained the sink.

The BIC diff at https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates/commit/43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138 adds lib/logging.js lines 89-92, where getRepoUrl(dep) is appended to the table row without sanitization, and adds lib/repo-url.js, whose direct-HTTPS branch returns the original gitURL string. git blame at the BIC attributes all four sink lines to 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138.

Direct-parent verification used the BIC object's sole parent 2ae1ed2d0573d086815dfb7d98e7ecc82aeb0a11 and a parent-tree git grep for repositoryLink|getRepoUrl|repoUrl under lib; it returned no matches. The BIC diff also shows lib/repo-url.js as a new file and the raw repoUrl table cells as additions, proving the vulnerable path is absent from the immediate parent.

Version-boundary checks show the BIC parent describes from v10.0.0, while the version-sorted tags containing the BIC begin at v10.1.0 and v10.1.0's package.json declares 10.1.0. The BIC is an ancestor of advisory-listed last-vulnerable tag v23.0.2. The fix is not an ancestor of v23.0.2, is an ancestor of v23.1.0, and the version-sorted tags containing it begin at v23.1.0; package.json at those tags declares 23.0.2 and 23.1.0 respectively.

The first-party fix commit https://github.com/raineorshine/npm-check-updates/commit/b554b84848fc0b08a9d2b3d3db15e351387168cf changes src/lib/logging.ts so both packageJson.homepage and getRepoUrl(...) pass through sanitizeForDisplay before entering the table. sanitizeForDisplay applies node:util stripVTControlCharacters and then removes remaining C0/C1 controls, including bare CR. The commit adds regression coverage for OSC in homepage and CR in repository data.

numactl-prefixed git cat-file -p inspected only the BIC commit object for attribution. It has one parent, human author/committer Jason O'Neill, and no trailers or AI/bot marker; therefore the proven smallest BIC has no commit-object AI attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerability is a source-to-sink failure: attacker-influenced metadata in an installed dependency's package.json is selected for an optional display column and then printed by the terminal table without control-sequence neutralization. History establishes two entry points into one flawed mechanism. The repository route is older: 43bac8b12f6cdbc121c11cc0839e97d7abba0138 both introduced getRepoUrl and directly inserted its result into the displayed row, so it is the smallest causal BIC rather than later renames, TypeScript moves, inline refactors, or the 2026 homepage expansion. Its sole direct parent's tree contains none of the repository-display symbols, and the introduced source file/table lines are additions. No squash decomposition is needed because this one-parent member commit itself contains the causal code rather than merely moving or aggregating an earlier implementation. The BIC entered release v10.1.0 and remained ancestral to v23.0.2. Commit b554b84848fc0b08a9d2b3d3db15e351387168cf directly closes both homepage and repository paths by sanitizing immediately before display and is first present in v23.1.0. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker, so BIC-only attribution requires NOT_AI regardless of later commits or the fix authorship.
